coboundary_analysis.description: For triviality, we need γ_gb = δf for some odd map f: g → g
coboundary_analysis.key_equation: (δf)(a_1^σ, b_j^s) = gb_{σ,j,s} · κ (up to adjoint representation)
coboundary_analysis.map_f_requirement: f must be odd (reverse parity) and satisfy specific commutation relations

theoretical.summary: Triviality of C(n+1) inhomogeneous gb deformation
theoretical.key_observation: The gb deformation introduces terms proportional to the odd central element κ in specific bracket relations. For triviality, we need a map f: g → g such that all generated coboundary terms match the gb deformation.

constraint_analysis.coboundary_range: The coboundary operator generates terms by commuting f(X) with elements of g. Since κ is central, [X, κ] = 0 for all X. This severely restricts what deformations can be coboundaries.
constraint_analysis.gb_structure: The gb parameters appear linearly in the deformed brackets as [b_j^s, a_1^σ] = -gb_{σ,j,s} · κ. A coboundary must reproduce these exact terms.
constraint_analysis.parity_argument: f must reverse parity. So f maps even elements to odd and vice versa. The map f(b_j^s) must be odd, and f(a_1^σ) must be even.

theoretical.theoretical_conclusion: The inhomogeneous gb deformation is GENERICALLY NON-TRIVIAL. For the deformation to be trivial, the gb parameters must satisfy very specific constraints. Analysis suggests that most configurations of gb parameters do NOT yield coboundaries.
theoretical.condition_for_triviality: A deformation with non-zero gb parameters can be trivial only if there exists an odd map f: g → g satisfying the coboundary equation. This imposes stringent algebraic constraints on the gb parameters.
